held_records.reason: Primary146 and secondary17 Q74 permits resulted in the expulsion and resulted from the expulsion. One makes expulsion an effect, the other a cause; the sentence supplies no chronology that excludes either.

Primary147 Q79 preserves to have failed and for failing, both valid after sorry in this sentence about yesterday. Secondary18 corrupts the first to to having failed. Hold rather than relying on the damaged alternative to force one answer.

Primary147 and secondary18 Q80/81 sequence offers he wanted, he wants and he does want after depended on what. Present forms may retain a still-current preference, so the sentence does not force backshift without further time context.
Primary147 and secondary18 Q82 repeats I am working and I’m working as equivalent choices. The punctuation joining busy to the next clause is also incomplete; no unique answer.
Primary148 and secondary18 Q83 allows started writing as well as had started writing before I arrived. Before already establishes sequence; past perfect is not mandatory.

Primary148 and secondary18 Q84 permits began to wane, was beginning to wane and was waning after the goals. These valid aspect choices describe different possible developments; no context uniquely selects one.
Primary148 and secondary18 Q85 offers costed and has costed with no explicit time boundary. The costed the initial value wording is itself awkward, so do not force a tense answer.
Primary148 and secondary18 Q87 admits a means to improve, a means of improving and a means for improving. These are standard ways of expressing a method or purpose; there is no unique completion.

Primary148–149 Q89 has any more advice and any advice, both valid uncountable constructions. Secondary18 corrupts the first to advices; keep private rather than treating that transcription error as proof of uniqueness.
